provenance: Synthetic example written by Claude for development. The reference marks are Claude's, not a teacher's. Replace with teacher-marked work before quoting agreement figures.
title: Cells and photosynthesis
subject: Science
schemeText:
Q1 Name the part of a plant cell where photosynthesis happens. (1) Chloroplast.
Q2 Write the word equation for photosynthesis. (2) carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen. 1 mark for correct reactants, 1 for correct products.
Q3 Name two structures found in plant cells but not animal cells. (2) Any two of: cell wall, chloroplast, permanent vacuole.
Q4 Why do plants need light for photosynthesis? (1) Light provides the energy for the reaction.
Q5 Suggest why a plant kept in the dark loses mass. (2) No photosynthesis so no glucose made (1); glucose still used in respiration (1).
pupilWork:
1) in the leaf
2) carbon dioxide + water = oxygen + sugar
3) cell wall, nucleus
4) to make food
5) because it has no light so it dies

reference.notes: Q2: 'sugar' accepted for glucose at KS3, so 2. Borderline; a stricter marker would give 1. Q4 and Q5 do not mention energy or glucose.

flags: Q2: the pupil wrote 'sugar' rather than 'glucose'. Check whether you accept it.
demoResult.feedback: You named the reactants of photosynthesis correctly and spotted the cell wall. Next, learn where photosynthesis happens inside the cell, and explain light as the energy source.

criteria.comment: Leaf is not the part of the cell; chloroplast needed.
Reactants correct; 'sugar' given instead of glucose.
Cell wall correct; nucleus is in animal cells too.
No reference to glucose, photosynthesis or respiration.
